chapter_theme: A song at Aththikkarai (அத்திக்கரை): the poet asks to leave the vanity of adornment and mean company, remove the three faults, learn faultlessly, serve the freed who know themselves, and enter the shoreless sea of release; the praise names the shakti that pierced the Suras and Valli rescued from the elephant.

896.reading: The poet asks not to wander on earth washing and decking the skin with gold and scent, proud, leaving purity and doing what the elders' words forbid among mean kin, but to remove the three faults, learn many arts without error, and, by the knowledge gained in serving the freed ones who know themselves, see the Real and enter the shoreless sea of release. The praise names the one shakti that pierced the Suras who had made the eight directions and the gods serve them, so that Indra's grief ended and he regained his city, Murugan who called the frightened kura girl when the elephant came and embraced her, and the dear son of Siva with water and the crescent in his hair, at Aththikkarai.
896.nuance: முக்குற்றம் அகற்றி: the three faults are traditionally desire, anger and delusion. தனையுணர் முத்தர்க்கு அடிமைப்பட்டு இலகிய அறிவாலே: knowledge comes through service to the freed, not by study alone. கரையகல் முத்திப்புணரி: release as a sea without a shore. கரி வரும் அத்தத்தில் அழைத்து: the elephant that frightened Valli into Murugan's arms.

links.note: The Kural says pain perishes when even the names of desire, anger and delusion perish; 896 asks to remove the three faults (முக்குற்றம்) as the first step toward the shoreless sea of release. The link depends on reading முக்குற்றம் as the Kural's three.
